11.title: Import Progress: report a determinate task
11.description: A lesson import has processed 4 of 10 files. Add a visible label and a progress element with value 4 and max 10; include fallback text that also communicates the count.
11.learningObjective: Use progress for a task that has a measurable completion value and a known maximum.
instructions: Add a label whose for value matches the progress id.
Set the progress value to 4 and max to 10.
Include the text 4 of 10 files processed inside the element.
Do not use progress for a static quality score.

workedExample.input: An import with four of ten files processed
workedExample.output: A labeled progress element with value 4 and max 10.
workedExample.explanation: progress describes completion of a task. The visible fallback remains helpful in browsers that do not show a native text label inside the control.

11.hint: A determinate progress element needs a value and a maximum to communicate its current completion.
11.explanation: progress describes completion of a task. The visible fallback remains helpful in browsers that do not show a native text label inside the control.
11.expectedOutput:
Import course files

4 of 10 files processed
11.expectedOutputHint: Visual reference only. HTML completion is reviewed against source requirements, not browser-executed tests.
11.starterCode: Import course files

12.title: Mastery Reading: use meter for a scalar value
12.description: A completed skills review gives a learner a mastery score of 82 on a 0–100 scale. Add a visible label and meter with min, max, low, high, optimum, and value. This is a score, not completion of an ongoing task.
12.learningObjective: Use meter to show a value within a known range, and distinguish it from task progress.
instructions: Connect a visible label to meter id mastery.
Set min 0, max 100, low 30, high 70, and optimum 90.
Set the value to 82.
Include fallback text with the numeric score.
Keep the explanation clear that meter represents a scalar measurement.

workedExample.input: A mastery score of 82 out of 100
workedExample.output: A labeled meter whose value is 82 in the declared range.
workedExample.explanation: meter represents a scalar value in a known range and can express low and high thresholds. Its meaning differs from progress, which reports task completion.

12.hint: Use meter for a known-range measurement such as a score; use progress for how much of a task is complete.
12.explanation: meter represents a scalar value in a known range and can express low and high thresholds. Its meaning differs from progress, which reports task completion.

testCases.description: Use a labeled meter, not progress.
Set the requested range and thresholds.
Include text that communicates the score.

12.expectedOutput:
Skills review

82%

13.title: Upload Notes: configure a file form safely
13.description: A learner uploads a CSV practice log. Use a file input with accept=".csv,text/csv" inside a form with enctype multipart/form-data. The server must inspect and validate the actual uploaded file.
13.learningObjective: Configure a file upload form with multipart encoding and communicate that client filters are not security checks.
instructions: Set the form method to post and enctype to multipart/form-data.
Add a visible label and a file input named practiceLog.
Set accept to .csv,text/csv as a chooser hint.
Add a submit button.
Do not claim accept validates file contents or makes an upload safe.

workedExample.output: A labeled file input and multipart form encoding.
workedExample.explanation: Multipart encoding carries file data in a form submission. Server code must validate size, content, and authorization because browser filters are only hints.

13.hint: The accept attribute can guide a file picker; a user can still send a different file directly.
13.explanation: Multipart encoding carries file data in a form submission. Server code must validate size, content, and authorization because browser filters are only hints.

testCases.description: Use a labeled file input named practiceLog.

14.title: Hidden Course ID: never trust a hidden field
14.description: A form carries courseId=python so the server can route a request. Add a hidden field with that name and value, but do not treat it as proof that the learner owns or may edit the course.
14.learningObjective: Add a named hidden input while recognizing that the submitted value is still controlled by the client.
instructions: Add an input with type hidden.
Set its name to courseId and value to python.
Keep the form’s visible submit action.
State that the server must verify the course against the authenticated user.

workedExample.input: A request for the Python course
workedExample.output: A named hidden field containing python plus a server-validation requirement.
workedExample.explanation: Hidden inputs are included in form data and can be changed by anyone who edits the request. Use them for transport convenience, never as authorization evidence.

14.hint: Hidden means not displayed by the browser; it does not mean secret or tamper-proof.
14.explanation: Hidden inputs are included in form data and can be changed by anyone who edits the request. Use them for transport convenience, never as authorization evidence.

testCases.description: Use type="hidden" with the exact name and value.
Keep the control inside the form.
Do not rely on its value for authorization.

14.expectedOutput: Continue learning
14.expectedOutputHint: Visual reference only. HTML completion is reviewed against source requirements, not browser-executed tests.
14.starterCode: Continue learning

15.title: Publish or Save Draft: override one submit destination
15.description: A lesson editor normally publishes to /lessons/publish. Add a second submit button that saves a draft to /lessons/draft while leaving the first button on the form’s default destination.
15.learningObjective: Use formaction to route one submit button differently from the form’s default action.
instructions: Set the form method to post and action to /lessons/publish.
Add a submit button for publishing without an override.
Add a second submit button for saving a draft.
Set formaction on only the draft button.
Keep both buttons inside the same form.

workedExample.input: One editor form with Publish and Save draft actions
workedExample.output: The draft button has formaction=/lessons/draft; the publish button inherits the form action.
workedExample.explanation: Submitter attributes allow one form to offer multiple destinations without duplicating its fields. The browser sends the action selected by the activated submit button.

15.hint: A submit button’s formaction overrides the form action for that submission only.
15.explanation: Submitter attributes allow one form to offer multiple destinations without duplicating its fields. The browser sends the action selected by the activated submit button.

testCases.description: Set formaction=/lessons/draft on the draft button only.

15.expectedOutput: Lesson editor
15.expectedOutputHint: Visual reference only. HTML completion is reviewed against source requirements, not browser-executed tests.
15.starterCode: Lesson editor
